angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 430,638 km at 39.61 pc = 0.15 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 25.2430 +/- 0.0126 mas (same row, RUWE 1.06): 39.61 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.619 +/- 0.019 solar radii from Bluhm et al. 2020, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1235 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...639A.132B/abstract): 430,638 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.63 +/- 0.024 solar masses from Bluhm et al. 2020, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1235 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...639A.132B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3997 +/- 51 K from Bluhm et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1235 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...639A.132B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bluhm et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1235 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...639A.132B/abstract)

ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1235 (pscomppars): age 5.3 Gyr, from Bluhm et al. 2020 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...639A.132B/abstract)
